- HIGH `[iterate-loop-name-resolution]`: Step 2 names exactly one test hazard for the moved `_run_iterate_convergence_loop` — the monkeypatch at `tests/cli/test_completeness_cmd.py:11074` — but that single fix is both incomplete and inconsistent with the plan's own "calls it unchanged" claim. recommendations.title: Several completeness_cmd.py-only helper functions and module constants that steps 3-5's relocated code depends on are ne
recommendations.body: Several completeness_cmd.py-only helper functions and module constants that steps 3-5's relocated code depends on are never given a new home, so following the plan's own stated line ranges leaves them stranded. `_apply_files_coherence` (completeness_cmd.py:941-1032, its only call site at line 471 inside step 4's ~377-507 range) sits outside every step's stated range (247-364, 377-507, 509-753, 756-927) — same for `_load_saved_data_contract_payloads` / `_data_contract_payload_target` / `_data_contract_completeness_redirect` (completeness_cmd.py:1057-1108, called at lines 366 and 662, which fall in steps 3 and 5) and `_completeness_apply_commit_subject` (completeness_cmd.py:935-939, called at lines 736 and 909, both in step 5), plus the constants the moved code reads: `_CONCEPTUAL_APPLY_SOURCE_RANK`, `_BARE_PLAN_WALKABLE_SOURCES`, `_DATA_CONTRACT_SOURCE`, `_DATA_CONTRACT_TARGET`, `_SAVED_SERIAL_APPLY_SOURCE_RANK` (completeness_cmd.py:1033-1056). Leaving any of these in completeness_cmd.py while their only caller moves to completeness_phases.py forces a back-import from phases to cmd — the exact cycle completeness_phases.py's own module docstring says must never exist (confirmed: completeness_phases.py imports nothing from completeness_cmd today). `_apply_files_coherence` is also on the same `from plan_tool.cli.completeness_cmd import (...)` block (test_completeness_cmd.py:69-77) as `_run_iterate_convergence_loop`, so getting its new home wrong breaks that whole import, not just its own call sites. Worse, `_data_contract_completeness_redirect` has its own test monkeypatch (`tests/cli/test_completeness_cmd.py:7049`, `monkeypatch.setattr(ccmd, "_data_contract_completeness_redirect", fake_redirect)`) that the plan's "four names" monkeypatch list (`walk_recommendations`, `working_tree_dirty`, `_apply_files_coherence`, `_build_review_action_fn`) never mentions, so the Risks section's claim that "steps 2, 4, and 5 each name their specific monkeypatch retargets explicitly" is false for this one.
recommendations.suggested_action: extend steps 3-5's scope to explicitly name where each of these local helpers and constants lands (naturally alongside the step that owns their sole caller), and add `_data_contract_completeness_redirect` as a fifth name to the monkeypatch-retarget list.

recommendations.title: Step 2 names exactly one test hazard for the moved `_run_iterate_convergence_loop` — the monkeypatch at `tests/cli/test_
recommendations.body: Step 2 names exactly one test hazard for the moved `_run_iterate_convergence_loop` — the monkeypatch at `tests/cli/test_completeness_cmd.py:11074` — but that single fix is both incomplete and inconsistent with the plan's own "calls it unchanged" claim. The test file imports `_run_iterate_convergence_loop` directly from `plan_tool.cli.completeness_cmd` in its module-level import block (line 73) and reuses that name in roughly 14 direct, unmocked calls (e.g. lines 7408, 8102, 8831, 9141, 10793, 10846, 10908, 10968, 11197, 11260, 11414, 11565, 12416, 12435) plus 6 `inspect.getsource(_run_iterate_convergence_loop)` checks (lines 7976, 7994, 8005, 8025, 8182, 11685) — none named anywhere in the plan, and since they share one import statement with several other names, a wrong call here fails that whole statement and the entire test file stops collecting. Separately, the loop's body (completeness_cmd.py:2787) calls `write_pre_apply_audit_checkpoint`, already correctly homed in `completeness_phases.py:488`; three tests patch `completeness_cmd.write_pre_apply_audit_checkpoint` to intercept that exact call (test lines 7393, 8818, 9118), and once the loop's body sits beside that function in the same file, the call resolves locally and those three patches go silent too. Whether any of this actually breaks turns on one design choice the plan never states: does `completeness_cmd.py` keep `_run_iterate_convergence_loop` importable as a bare name (which would satisfy every site above with zero change, but would also mean the monkeypatch at line 11074 keeps working unmodified — patches intercept through the *caller's* namespace, and `cmd_completeness`, the caller, never moves), or does it call through a qualified `completeness_phases.` reference (the only reading under which the stated monkeypatch retarget is actually necessary, and under which every site above breaks)? The plan asserts the retarget is needed without saying which design produces that need, so the sites that choice implies are never named.
recommendations.suggested_action: state explicitly whether completeness_cmd.py re-imports the moved function's bare name or calls it via a qualified reference, and name the resulting site list (either "the one monkeypatch, nothing else" or the ~20 test-file sites plus the three `write_pre_apply_audit_checkpoint` patches) so step 2's hazard enumeration matches whichever choice is made.

The closure exists specifically to print the audit-shape advisory exactly once via `nonlocal advisory_presented` — its own comment calls this a guard against "a worker/replay duplicate." Once steps 3 and 5 become separate functions in completeness_phases.py, whichever one step 3 becomes has to hand this exact closure (or the mutable state behind it) to whatever step 5 becomes, and nothing in the plan says so — an implementer following the plan's explicit state inventory alone has no reason to preserve it as one shared closure rather than, say, two independently-tracked flags that could double-print the advisory.
recommendations.suggested_action: add `_present_pre_apply_advisory` (and the `pre_apply_advisory_display` / `advisory_presented` state it closes over) to the Architecture section's list of state that must cross the step 3 → step 5 boundary by reference, not by copy.

recommendations.body: Step 5 claims ownership of retargeting all four `completeness-apply` monkeypatches (`walk_recommendations`, `working_tree_dirty`, `_apply_files_coherence`, `_build_review_action_fn`), but two of the four gate code that step 4, not step 5, actually relocates. `_apply_files_coherence`'s only call site sits inside step 4's own stated "~440–507 files-coherence apply/skip" range, and the two tests the plan names for `working_tree_dirty` (`test_dirty_tree_refused`, `test_tty_without_yes_refused`) both pass `--jobs 2` and exercise only the clean-tree check inside step 4's own stated "~377–507 `--jobs`/`--parallel` decision" range — a different call than the `working_tree_dirty` calls further down that do belong to step 5's range. If step 4 lands with these two retargets deferred to step 5 as currently written, these three tests fail the moment step 4's own commit lands, before step 5 starts — contradicting the plan's own "green before completion" per-step testing rule and the acceptance criterion that ties monkeypatch retargets only to steps 2 and 5.
recommendations.suggested_action: move the `_apply_files_coherence` retarget and the clean-tree-gate `working_tree_dirty` retarget into step 4's own intent, and add step 4 to the acceptance criterion listing which steps retarget monkeypatches; step 5 keeps owning `walk_recommendations`, `_build_review_action_fn`, and `working_tree_dirty`'s other, later call sites.
